I reviewed the uncommitted diff and reported seven findings. I didn't run the test suite. All the findings come from reading the diff and grepping `lib/` and `index.d.ts` for leftover `AxiosError.call`, `inherits` and `toFlatObject` callers. I found none inside the repo.

All of them are regressions from rewriting `AxiosError` and `CanceledError` as ES classes:

1. **`AxiosError.from` (`lib/core/AxiosError.js:6`)**
   - It no longer copies the original error's own properties, such as `errno`, `syscall`, `address` and `port` on Node network errors.
   - It lost the old fallbacks to the message and name 'Error'.
   - It now throws a TypeError if `error` is null or undefined.
   - `code || error.code` also treats a falsy code differently from the old `code == null` check.
2. **`cause` (`lib/core/AxiosError.js:9`)**: It is now an enumerable own property. It used to be non-enumerable on purpose, to keep JSON and log output clean.
3. **`status` (`lib/core/AxiosError.js:34`)**: `this.status = response.status` drops the old `null` fallback. A response with no status now gives `undefined` instead of `null`.
4. **`isAxiosError` (`lib/core/AxiosError.js:29`)**: It is now an own, enumerable, writable property. It used to be a non-enumerable property on the prototype.
5. **Static error codes (`lib/core/AxiosError.js:58`)**: `ERR_*`, `ECONNABORTED` and `ETIMEDOUT` were non-writable and non-enumerable. They are now ordinary assignable properties, so they can be overwritten.
6. **`__CANCEL__` (`lib/cancel/CanceledError.js:19`)**: It moved from the prototype to an enumerable own property on every instance, which shows up in `Object.keys` and equality assertions.
7. **`new` required (`lib/core/AxiosError.js:16`)**: Both classes now need `new`. Third-party code that uses `AxiosError.call(this, ...)` with `utils.inherits` will throw "Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'".

findings.summary: The rewritten `AxiosError.from` no longer copies the original error's own properties and no longer has the old fallbacks.
findings.failure_scenario: The old code used `toFlatObject` to copy the source error's own properties. A Node network error such as ECONNREFUSED carries `errno`, `syscall`, `address` and `port`, and these are now lost. The old code also fell back to the message 'Error' and the name 'Error'. If `error` is null or undefined, the new code throws a TypeError on `error.message`. `code || error.code` also treats an empty or falsy code differently from the old `code == null` check.

findings.summary: `cause` is now set by plain assignment, so it is an enumerable own property. The old code made it non-enumerable on purpose to avoid JSON and log noise.
findings.failure_scenario: `Object.keys(err)`, a spread of the error, or a deep-equal comparison now includes `cause`. The `cause` can be a large Node error, and this can change serialised or logged output.

findings.summary: `this.status = response.status` drops the old `response.status ? response.status : null` normalisation.
findings.failure_scenario: If a response has no status, `err.status` is now `undefined` instead of `null`. Code or tests that check `=== null` break.

findings.summary: `isAxiosError` is now an own, enumerable, writable instance property. It used to be a non-enumerable prototype property.
findings.failure_scenario: `isAxiosError` now shows up in `Object.keys`, spread copies and `toEqual` comparisons of errors. It can also be overwritten. Instances that are copied or serialised and rebuilt keep the flag when they shouldn't.

findings.summary: The static error codes (`ERR_*`, `ECONNABORTED`, `ETIMEDOUT`) were non-writable and non-enumerable. They are now ordinary assignable and enumerable properties.
findings.failure_scenario: Code can reassign `AxiosError.ERR_CANCELED = 'x'`, which silently changes the behaviour of every check that uses it. The codes also now show up when iterating the class's keys.

findings.summary: `__CANCEL__` moved from the prototype to an own enumerable property set in the constructor.
findings.failure_scenario: Every `CanceledError` instance now has an enumerable `__CANCEL__` key. This shows up in `Object.keys` and in object-equality assertions. It also changes the behaviour of any code that relied on the flag living on the prototype.

findings.summary: Both classes now require `new`, so the old `AxiosError.call(this, ...)` and `utils.inherits` subclassing pattern throws "Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'". This is a breaking change for third-party code.
findings.failure_scenario: Code outside the repo that does `function MyErr(){ AxiosError.call(this, ...) }; utils.inherits(MyErr, AxiosError)` now throws a TypeError. A grep of `lib/` found no remaining internal callers, so this affects only external users. The change is also not noted in any changelog.
